newsitem.title: FINLAND: Europeans ignorant of diabetes risk, survey finds.
newsitem.headline: Europeans ignorant of diabetes risk, survey finds.

text.p: Most Europeans do not know that being overweight can lead to diabetes and heart disease, a survey released on Monday found.
Up to four out of five did not know about the link with diabetes, while awareness of heart disease varied country by country, the survey found.

Only 22 percent of the 6,000 people questioned on behalf of Knoll Pharmaceuticals mentioned diabetes when asked what health risks could arise from obesity. Even when asked specifically about obesity 52 percent failed to see the link.
"Thirty-six percent failed to mention heart disease, the most publicised health hazard of being obese," Knoll said in a statement.
Italians seemed most aware of the risk, with 31 percent of the 1,000 questioned saying they knew being overweight could lead to diabetes.
The worst-informed were the Dutch, with only nine percent of the 1,000 people questioned in the Netherlands making the link.
Obesity is defined as being about 20 percent above ideal weight or having a body mass index -- height in metres squared divided by weight in kilograms -- of 30 or more.
Obese people are more than 26 times more likely to have diabetes than people who are of normal weight and are 3.5 times more likely to die of heart disease.
About 80 percent of people with type-two, or non-insulin- dependent diabetes, are classified as obese when diagnosed.
